Prove each equivalence by showing both sides are independently true.

The main representation is
\[
T_n(\cos \theta)=\cos(n\theta).
\]
Thus at \(\theta=k\pi/n\), the value is \((-1)^k\). Combine this with the extremal bound \(-1\le T_n(x)\le1\) for \(x\in[-1,1]\). Odd \(k\) therefore gives a global minimum on \([-1,1]\). Even \(k\) gives value \(1\); the strict assumptions \(0<k<n\) place \(\cos(k\pi/n)\) in \((-1,1)\), so the interval bound applies on a whole neighborhood and yields a local maximum.

For the other two assertions, use the standard negative-index symmetry of the second-kind Chebyshev polynomials,
\[
U_{-n}=-U_{n-2},
\]
which follows from their integer-index recurrence and is valid over every commutative ring, and use that Chebyshev’s \(\psi(x)\) has no prime-power contributions below \(2\), hence \(\psi(x)=0\) for \(x<2\). Existing library lemmas for these identities, the cosine evaluation, and the extremal bound should reduce the proof to parity simplification and elementary interval membership.
